fun_highlights: The bequest card (e_bequest) is a genuine inter-generational lever: choosing 'Everything I know' vs 'Nothing but their own freedom' visibly shapes the heir's starting stats and the opening text of the next life. This is the closest thing to actual dynasty strategy in the game, and it lands well in Dynasty 13/Lindqvist where Anders's 'freedom' bequest produces a distinctly looser Gen 5 opening.

Era-gated content creates real macro-variety. In Dynasty 4/Okonkwo the war era produces a draft card (w_war_call) and a war-loss card in back-to-back generations; in Dynasty 6/Thorne the plague era generates the sickness-tending decision multiple times across different lives, each with a different resolution. A house genuinely lives through changing times.

The vocation arc system works: a soldier's life has 'a_soldier_service' / 'm_soldier_ghost' / 'e_soldier_old'; a maker has the shop-gamble, the masterwork, the handoff. In Dynasty 13 Gen 4 (Mateo, soldier), the war-ghost card at 48 ('the war comes back at three in the morning') and the elder truth-of-soldiering card at 75 give the life a recognisable through-line absent from non-soldiers.

The house aspirations readout ('Still ahead: a place in the histories, words the family can live by') and the houseCharacter function give a dynasty strategist a legible trajectory. The heir screen surfaces this explicitly, and in long-running dynasties (Okonkwo, Castellane, Lindqvist) the seat-climb combined with motto-crystallisation produces a real arc: a rented room rises to a fine townhouse with 'What we have, we share.' stamped on it.

Callback cards that reach decades back ('cb_lookaway', 'cb_books_late', 'cb_first_loss') are among the most emotionally effective moments in the transcripts. The callback architecture is the right instinct — when they fire (Beatrix Okonkwo at 47 returning the family book; Hale at 50 stopping for the person he once walked past), the game earns its meditative label.

The seat-gated and repute-gated cards ('s_great_burden', 'r_scholar_door', 'r_hard_name', 's_patronage') give a strategist meaningful things to build toward: a scholarly house unlocks a 'carry the learning further' card; a ruthless house meets 'r_name_cost' forcing a reckoning. These are exactly the kind of dynasty-reactive moments the genre needs.
staleness: The marriage prompt fires in nearly every adult life with near-identical framing variations. Across 15 dynasties, 'Ask. Build a life.' / 'Not yet. Maybe never.' appears in roughly 30 individual lives. The phrasing pools are large, but the prompt shape — love interest present, marriage pending, same two-option structure — is so consistent that it reads as a template tax, not a moment. Dynasties 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15 all show this within one or two generations of one another.

The reputation card 'a_make_name' (age 30-52, 'be known as learned/hard to cross/open-handed') fires in an enormous fraction of adult lives and produces near-identical outcome lines: 'Set out, deliberately, to be the one no one tried twice.' In Dynasty 1 (Saoirse, age 44), Dynasty 2 (Henrik, age 38), Dynasty 5 (Ottilie, age 15 variant), Dynasty 6/Thorne Gen 1 and 3, and multiple Lindqvist lives, the exact same phrasing recurs within readable distance of one another. As a dynasty strategist, this also fails tactically: the card steers reputation but its once-per-life fire means a strategist gets one shot to push the house's character and then has no further lever until the next generation.

The 's_from_nothing' card ('There is nothing behind you — no name that means a thing') fires in nearly every dynasty that starts at seat 0-1, which is most of them, with identical text and identical two-choice outcome ('Build, brick by brick' / 'Find others to climb with'). It appears verbatim in Dynasties 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 12, 13, 14, 15. Because all dynasties start at seat 1, this is effectively a universal early-adult event wearing a situational costume.

Elder body-decline observations (vit_tire, vit_neg pools) are very deep in lines but structurally identical in function across every long life. In Dynasty 13/Anders (Gen 3) and Dynasty 13/Mateo (Gen 4), the body-declining observation fires as a passive line ('Each day now asks a little more of him') and then 'e_body' fires as an interactive card ('push on regardless / slow down'), within the same life. The passive-then-interactive double-hit on the same theme makes the elder arc feel schematic. In the transcripts nearly every life over 60 runs: body observation, e_body card, e_peace card, e_legacy card. The rhythm is visible.

The maternal/paternal death events ('Lost his mother', 'Lost her father') recur with no prose variation — the event is simply a one-line log entry. In Dynasty 4/Okonkwo alone: Calla loses father at 58, mother at 62; Elias loses mother at 41, father at 68; Noor loses father at 44, mother at 48; Beatrix loses mother at 40, father at 60; Hale loses mother at 36, father at 59. These are extremely high-frequency and entirely undifferentiated — no card, no choice, no prose weight beyond 'Lost X.' For a dynasty strategist these are noise that occupies log space without adding anything.

Dynasty-level strategic agency is thin in practice. The only direct seat levers are: earn peak means >= 80 (automatic on death), invest via 'm_invest_name' (a single midlife card with 62% success rate), and avoid 'facedReckoning=fell'. There is no card that lets a strategist choose the house's ERA strategy, deliberately sacrifice seat for reputation, or make a multi-generational investment. The 'Still ahead' aspirations text names goals but offers no active path to most of them. A player who wants to 'play the house' discovers that most dynasty outcomes are determined by stat drift and card luck, not deliberate choices.

improvements.what: Add 1-2 explicit dynasty-strategy cards per generation that target the house directly — a 'founding-investment' card at founding (spend means to lock in a starting reputation direction), a 'generational-pact' card mid-dynasty (commit the family to a 10-year austerity or expansion that makes the next heir's start conditions visibly different), or a 'succession-dispute' card that lets the current life shape WHO inherits rather than only WHAT.
improvements.why: Currently the only cross-generational lever a strategist has is the bequest card (which fires once per life) and indirect stat-building. Real dynasty strategy requires more deliberate 'play the house not the person' moments. The existing 's_inheritance_dispute' and 'm_invest_name' cards show the right instinct but aren't enough. A player who finishes Dynasty 4/Okonkwo's 5-generation arc has no memory of making a dynasty-scale decision beyond bequests.

improvements.what: Make parent deaths carry at least one optional reactive card (perhaps firing within 1-3 years of the log line) with a choice: 'Grieve it properly' vs 'Absorb it and move on.' Specifically for the lineage-echo parent (who the player lived as), a brief moment of reckoning when the previous life officially dies would reinforce the dynasty continuity feel. The current bare 'Lost his mother, Calla.' at line 257 for Elias Okonkwo is the flattest moment in a genre where those deaths should land hard.
improvements.why: Parent deaths are among the highest-frequency events across all 15 dynasties and currently carry zero weight or choice. For a dynasty-focused player, losing the previous self-character to age should be a notable moment, not a one-line log entry.

improvements.what: Gate 'a_make_name' behind a check that the house does NOT already have a strong leading reputation (e.g. repute top value < 0.8) and increase its onceDyn cooldown to 4-5. Compensate by adding a second reputation-steering card that fires later (midlife) allowing course-correction or doubling-down. Currently a strategist gets one weak reputation push per life with no feedback loop.
improvements.why: The card as written is both over-frequent (fires in almost every adult life because the condition is trivially met) and underweight for its strategic importance. The dynasty-strategist lens demands this be a meaningful, legible lever — and right now it reads as just another adult filler card.

improvements.what: Differentiate parent-death text by the quality of the bond: a high-bond parent death (bond > 65) should trigger a distinct, warmer log line; a low-bond parent death (bond < 35) should trigger a cooler or more complicated one. One sentence of differentiation is all it takes to stop the event feeling like a procedural timer.
improvements.why: Relationship bonds are tracked with real precision throughout each life, but their values are never surfaced in the most emotionally significant event the relationship system produces. This is a straightforward use of existing data.

improvements.what: Add a house-level 'living with the motto' card that fires once per generation AFTER the motto crystallizes — presenting a moment where the current life must either honor the family words at personal cost or break with them, with downstream reputation effects. Dynasty 4/Okonkwo Gen 5 has a weaker version of this (Hale honoring Calla at 29), but it's a cb card gated on a memory, not a consistent dynasty-layer event. The motto should regularly ask something of the lives that carry it.
improvements.why: The motto is the dynasty's most legible identity artifact, but it currently functions as pure flavor text after crystallization. A strategist building toward 'By our own hands' or 'We do not save ourselves for later' should feel that identity as a constraint and an advantage, not just a header. The existing 'a_family_words' card (Anders Lindqvist Gen 5, age 62) is the right shape but fires only once.

verdict: A Life has genuine structural bones — the vocation arcs, callback system, era-gating, and bequest lever are real and produce meaningfully different lives in the transcripts. But as a dynasty strategy game it is currently a witness more than a player: the house accumulates seat and reputation through largely automatic stat-to-outcome mappings, the deliberate cross-generational levers are sparse (one bequest card, one invest-name card, one make-name card per life), and the two highest-frequency events in any long session — marriage and parent death — are so templated that by dynasty 4 they read as procedural overhead rather than meaningful beats. The staleness is not in the writing quality, which is consistently high, but in the strategic architecture: a player who wants to steer a house across five generations discovers they have very few actual steering decisions, and the ones they have tend to be the same decisions repeated across every life in the dynasty.
